lead.title: Cambridge's T-Therapeutics raises $133M Series B to take two TCR-CD3 bispecifics into the clinic
lead.deck: The round is co-led by Advent Life Sciences and the British Business Bank, with JJDC (J&J Innovation), Samsara BioCapital, M Ventures and Eli Lilly joining; Sofinnova, Sanofi Ventures and Tencent follow on. Proceeds will bring two programmes — solid tumours and autoimmunity — from the OpTiMus fully human TCR platform into trials.

milestone.title: Lytix: Phase II NeoLIPA study meets its primary endpoint in resectable melanoma
milestone.summary: The Norwegian company says NeoLIPA met its primary pathological complete response endpoint (November 2 release; detailed figures not reviewed).
milestone.why: A Phase II primary endpoint met is the kind of catalyst that precedes a partnership or a raise; the detailed data remain to be examined.

deal.thesis: Oxford spin-out (Adam Mead, Beth Psaila) built around ATX-011, an anti-G6B monoclonal antibody for essential thrombocythaemia; round co-led by Sofinnova Partners and RA Capital, with Oxford Science Enterprises, Cancer Research Horizons and the University of Oxford, to advance into Phase 1/2a.

brefsEurope.summary: The offer follows Egetis' $190M sale of its rare pediatric priority review voucher (PRV) a day earlier — a useful comparable on PRV value.

brefsEurope.title: Abera Bioscience cleared by Dutch authorities for a Phase I trial of its nasal pneumococcal vaccine
brefsEurope.summary: First-in-human trial of a nasally administered pneumococcal vaccine candidate.

brefsEurope.summary: Nxera Pharma, which holds rights in Japan and parts of Asia Pacific excluding China, pays CHF 7M on exercising an existing option; Idorsia stays eligible for royalties.

brefsEurope.title: Camurus doses first patient in Phase IIb study of its monthly semaglutide depot in obesity
brefsEurope.summary: Placebo-controlled study of the long-acting semaglutide depot, given once a month.

brefsEurope.summary: Alentis gets an exclusive option to in-license PinotBio's linkers and/or payloads; upfront undisclosed, plus milestones and royalties.

brefsEurope.summary: The round combines seed capital with non-dilutive Norwegian research funding.

word.fr: The PRV is a “coupon” the FDA gives a biotech whose rare pediatric disease drug has just been approved. It speeds up review of another filing and, above all, can be resold: about $190M at Egetis in early November 2026.
word.definition: A voucher granted by the FDA on approval of a rare pediatric disease treatment, entitling the holder to priority review of another product and which can be sold to a third party.

parts.label: Trigger
parts.role: FDA approval of a product for a rare pediatric disease: the sponsor can then obtain a voucher (a “rare pediatric disease” designation can be requested before filing).

parts.label: The voucher
parts.role: A transferable asset: it can be used to obtain priority review of another product, or be sold to another sponsor.

parts.label: Legal framework
parts.role: Programme reinstated on February 3, 2026 by the Consolidated Appropriations Act 2026; the FDA can no longer award vouchers after September 30, 2029.

how.t: The biotech gets an FDA approval for a rare pediatric disease product. Egetis received its voucher on September 28, 2026 with the approval of EMCITATE (tiratricol) in MCT8 deficiency.
The voucher speeds up review of another product. A small biotech with no other filing ready sells it to a buyer who pays cash.

The sale is an asset transfer subject to closing conditions, including expiry of the US Hart-Scott-Rodino antitrust waiting period. Prices cited in 2026 range from $180M to $210M. At Egetis, about 50% of the net goes to RTTI's former owners (earn-out).

word.why: For an investor it is non-dilutive return attached to a regulatory success. A $190M sale funds several years of R&D without issuing shares and weighs on a small biotech's valuation. Two due-diligence points: earn-out or royalty clauses (Egetis passes on about 50% of the net) and the legal window (the FDA will issue no more vouchers after September 30, 2029). Another limit: the buyer is not always named.

startups.name: Egetis Therapeutics (Suède, cotée)
startups.use: Voucher obtained September 28, 2026 with FDA approval of EMCITATE; sale agreement announced November 4, 2026 for $190M gross (about SEK 1.9B), buyer unnamed, subject to HSR waiting-period expiry; about 50% of net owed to RTTI's former owners.
startups.place: Independent to date, but ANI Pharmaceuticals launched a recommended public offer on November 5, 2026 ($1.13 per share; acceptance period planned November 20 to December 18, 2026): not acquired until the offer closes.

startups.name: Denali Therapeutics (États-Unis, cotée)
startups.use: Voucher received after FDA approval of Avlayah (tividenofusp alfa) in Hunter syndrome in March 2026; sale announced June 18, 2026 for $195M gross, buyer undisclosed, to fund the TransportVehicle pipeline.
startups.place: Outside Europe, as no sale by another European biotech could be verified. No acquisition found in searches.
